Close the gap between “I need something” and “staff knows.”

QRK in three words

Quick. Responsive. Connected.

The product is designed around a faster service loop, not just a prettier digital menu.

01 · QUICK

Less waiting.

Customers can act the moment they are ready — order, refill, request, bill — without waiting for someone to notice them.

02 · RESPONSIVE

Staff know instantly.

Each request arrives with table context, request type, and wait time so the team can prioritize and fulfill instead of monitoring.

03 · CONNECTED

One table layer.

Customer → table → staff → kitchen → POS → owner. QRK sits in the middle and gives every side the same live context.

Starts with the menu. Grows into the table OS.

One lightweight layer above the systems you already use.

QRK should not force a restaurant to rip out its POS or relearn its operation. It becomes the digital surface customers touch and the service layer staff respond to.

↻

Always-current menu

Change prices, photos, variants, promos, and sold-out items once. The same printed QR immediately reflects the current menu.

＋

More chances to sell

Drinks, sides, dessert, upgrades, and extra items stay one tap away after the first order — without waiting for another order-taking round.

⚡

Lightweight customer side

No install, no account, and no unnecessary interface. The guest experience is optimized around opening quickly even on slower connections.

◎

Service analytics

Build toward request time, acknowledgment, fulfillment, busy periods, frequently requested items, and table behavior — useful operational signals, not vanity charts.

⇄

POS-compatible by direction.

QRK sits above the restaurant's existing stack. Orders can bridge into supported POS systems such as Loyverse through provider-specific connectors instead of making the business replace what already works.

FAQ

What QRK actually changes at the table.

No. The customer scans the table QR and opens the experience in the mobile browser. QRK is intentionally designed to keep the first interaction extremely light.
No. The point is to make staff more effective. QRK removes the monitoring and communication delay so waiters can spend more time actually serving tables.
One-tap table requests such as Meat Refill, Water, Rice, Side Dishes, Change Grill, Tissue, Call Staff, or Request Bill. Restaurants can tailor the actions to their service model.
Yes. Table-aware codes give each order or service request location context so staff instantly know where it came from.
That is the integration direction. QRK should sit above the restaurant's current stack and use a provider-specific bridge when the POS exposes a supported API or integration path.
Mark it unavailable from the owner side and the customer-facing menu can reflect the change immediately, with no QR reprint.
